description: Light and fast, the RedFox Speedy Kayak is an outstanding angling companion to outmaneuver any lake, river or creek. Sleek and sneaky by design, this may not be the sturdiest and most durable vessel, but the RedFox ensures a superb combination of quality, performance and stability to make you fast king of the current whatever the conditions may be!

name: MagFin™ SunFish Comfy Kayak
description: Easy to handle on and off the water, the SunFish Comfy Kayak is perfectly suited for beginners eager to take their angling experience a step further and explore new limits as well as those who appreciate maximum comfort in whatever they do! This super comfortable vessel will have you feeling rested and relaxed while providing a wonderful combination of performance and stability within delightfully compact size and design.

name: MagFin™ BlueWhale Endura Kayak
description: Wherever you angling adventures take you, the BlueWhale Endura Kayak is the one angling companion whose true grit you can really count on. Built with a backbone, BlueWhale’s philosophy is all about making haste slowly! Unmatched durability and stable performance of this somewhat heavy fishing vessel make up for where it lacks in speed and swiftness and will have you feeling safe and secure whatever the conditions may be! Taking is slowly, the no hassle BlueWhale Endura Kayak is tough indeed and built to last!

name: MagFin™ Santa’s Sleigh Kayak
description: Ho ho ho! Great for lakes and rivers, this fun kayak lifts up your spirits with unique collectible Christmas design, decorated to look like a real Santa's Sleigh! Built from high quality material that is durable, this kayak features large seating area with soft thigh pads for ultimate comfort and coziness on cold winter days, making Santa’s Sleigh the perfect kayaking companion to spend the holidays with if you’re planning to do some Christmas fishing!

name: MagFin™ MagFin™ DottedShark™ Sports Kayak
description: MagFin™ MagFin™ DottedShark™ Sports Kayak

name: MagFin™ Elven Kayak
description: This fantastic fairy-tale Elven kayak is a real work of art that you can actually take out for a Christmas fishing ride! Durable high-density materials and ergonomic construction provide enough comfort for stable paddling to make fishing on this Elven kayak truly enjoyable! But most importantly, this vessel’s unique collectible design is decorated by adorable Christmas elves, better known as Santa’s helpers, bringing you closer to the Christmas jingle-bells magic!

name: MagFin™ MagFin™ RedRiverDragon™
description: This collectible editions kayak is a fantastic angling companion whose speed, agility and power can outmaneuver any current! Part of our new Golden Dragon Pack, the RedRiverDragonkayak stands up to its name, letting you take your angling experience a step further and explore new limits with the Dragon power on your side!

name: MagFin™ Monstrosity
description: The curse of Fankenfish is broken and the vile monster is conquered! All thanks to you! This unique kayak bears the Head of the Frankenfish on it’s bow, as a horrendously magnificent decoration, a proud ornamenting sign of your heroic Triumph that will be remembered for ages to come!

name: MagFin™ Golden Kayak™
description: This magnificent top-quality kayak, with a fantastic smokey black&gold finish, was designed exclusively for the elite grade Golden FP Pack! Fast and super comfortable, this golden child of boatbuilding provides the skillful rower with great controls, superb maneuverability, and overall exceptional performance.

name: MagFin™ X-SERIES™ Pro Kayak
description: Behold the ultimate champion-level angling kayak, from the X-SERIES™ professional line! They say the best things money can’t buy - and that’s just the case with the limited edition X-SERIES™ Pro Kayak that can only be won by the champion of a kayak fishing tournament! The fastest and most maneuverable and of them all, this kayak ensures excellent controls and features recognizable badass design that make it apparent - this vessel is truly superior to all the rest!

name: MagFin™ TWKC Impetuous Kayak
description: Ever dreamed of your own vessel? This exclusive limited edition kayak made especially for the Topwater Kayak Cup will make your dream come true! Speed, maneuverability, and ease of control — what more could you ask for an angler who prefers to fish not on the bustling shores, but surrounded with peaceful waters? Except for the catchy, memorable design in the style of the tournament, which stands out brightly among many other faceless kayaks.

name: Native American Canoe
description: This unique canoe is very different from other boats you may come across on the reservoir. This is not surprising: it’s made using technologies invented by Native Americans hundreds of years ago.

name: Kayak Irish Rover
description: The carefree Irish Rover is ready to travel across any body of water and take you to the best fishing spots without any problems. This boat is quite heavy and not very elegant, but as strong as a barrel of the best Irish beer! It will help you feel confident, comfortable, and calm on the water.

name: Anniversary Trolling Kayak
description: Let’s celebrate Fishing Planet Anniversary aboard the Anniversary Trolling Kayak, sporting a one-of-a-kind festive look that stands out on the water! Its pedal-powered control keeps your hands free and removes the need for stamina-recovery pauses, so you can stay focused on trolling. Two extra rod holders and a built-in Echo Sounder give you everything you need to stay on the fish and maximize your haul!

name: Witching Recipe Book
description: This ancient magic book old as time itself contains countless spells, rituals and potions. There’s got to be at least a hundred different summoning potion recipes here! And one of them is just what we need to summon the Frankenfish.

name: Mandrake Root
description: Often used in magic rituals, the human-shaped poisonous roots of the Mandragora plant are a key ingredient in the Frankenfish summoning potion from the Witching Recipe Book.

name: Bunch of Mandrake Roots
description: Now you can add this bunch of Mandrake Roots to the summoning potion in the Witching Cauldron!

name: Jar of Fish Eyes
description: A whole jar of creepy fish eyes that apparently have magic powers. These were taken specifically from a Bowfin caught after midnight using Roaches as bait. An important ingredient in the Frankenfish summoning potion, according to the Witching Recipe Book.

name: Skeleton Tail
description: A magic skeleton tail from a Skeleton Bluegill that was caught in one of the planetary power places! According to the Quanchkin Witch’s book, this is an important ingredient of any summoning potion.

name: Green Ogre Scale
description: Bright green and sparkly, the scales of a Green Ogre gar have a very unique shade of green, hardly discernible by the human eye. Just the color that has to be added to the summoning potion, according the Witching Recipe Book.

name: Albino Yeti Gills
description: These magic fish gills taken from a real Albino Yeti gar should help our summoning potion absorb the breath of life and exhale, letting out all of its magic summoning powers!

name: Black Vampire Fin
description: Summoning potions usually require a Vampire's wing taken from a real Vampire in bat form! Luckily, to summon the Frankenfish, it’s enough to use a fin taken from a Vampire gar. Last but not least, this is the final ingredient!

name: Ghost Essence
description: Ghost essence is a key component of all summoning potions. But to summon a fish monster, you need the essence of a fish ghost! And this ethereal matter taken from an actual Ghost Pike is just the thing to summon Frankenfish!

name: Mad-Eye Buffalo Mount
description: Mad-Eye Buffalo (Ictiobus Oculus) Considered to be a figment of some anglers’ imagination, the Mad-Eye Buffalo is nevertheless very real and is in fact a rare and extremely strange mutation of the freshwater Smallmouth Buffalo. This monstrous fish gets its name for having magically sharp eyesight that, legend has it, allows it to see through anything - from walls to the human soul. It can also spot the most intricate details in any light, which means, that catching this monster will require using some of the thinnest and frailest fishing like you can find! Quite a challenge, considering that the Mad-Eye weighs around 13 lb. (6 kg)!!

name: Dendrofin Mount
description: Dendrofin (Amia Dendronimus) this extremely fishy mutation of what used to be your ordinary Bowfin is the result of an ambush predator going vegan! After all, you are what you eat! Or so they say. At least, the Dendrofin would agree. Looks like this particular specimen swapped his ordinary carnivorous diet for genuine tree bark and now miraculously resembles an old log! Gotta hand it to the vegan diet - this powerful monster has grown to nearly 13 lb (6 kg) and is getting stronger by the day! Who cares how you look when you’re that big, right? But while sporting such a tree-like texture might be Dendrofin’s great camouflage, we sure know what kind of bait this wood-hungry monster won’t resist!

name: Tyrannotrout Mount
description: Tyrannotrout (Oncorhynchus Tyrannosaurus) a.k.a the T-Rex Trout, is a carnivorous prehistoric monster of the Salmon family that has inexplicably infested the waters of one of New York’s most calm and peaceful lakes! Being a fairly small fish of under 2 lb (1 kg), a single T-Rex Trout couldn’t do much harm. Except from, maybe, biting your hand off. However, these razor-toothed flesh-hungry monsters hunt in schools and are endangering the entire population of fish in Rocky Lake! As there’s plenty of easy prey for these beasts to devour, the only way to get a Tyrannotrout’s attention is by using a special turtle-shell prehistoric lure.

name: Pikeslasher Mount
description: Pikeslasher (Sander Murderus) a genuine mystery to ichthyologists, the Pikeslasher is a blood-thirsty mutation of the common Walleye that has developed quite a taste for Pike! Who knows, perhaps this is a fishy case of personal vendetta, a thrilling story of Walleye vengeance for a loved one that was heartlessly, yet naturally, consumed by Pike sometime in the past... We’ll probably never know the Pikeslasher’s true motives. But what we do know, is that this gigantic carnivorous monster has adopted the coloration of a Pike and now weighs about 22 lb (10 kg)! Looks like you’ll need to make some first rate pike cutbait to trick the Pikeslasher into biting.

name: Eldergar Mount
description: Eldergar (Lepisosteus Antiquus) is probably the oldest known Longnose Gar ever recorded. Having well outlived the typical lifespan of its own species, the Eldergar at least 70 years old, which is twice the age of the oldest specimen previously recorded! No wonder this old-timer is also the largest Longnose in history - weighing almost 55 lb! (25 kg). Ichthyologists believe the reason behind this anomaly to be found in the Eldergar’s feeding habits. It appears that this old-timer has taken to a very strange diet: not only does the Eldergar hunt exclusively on American Shad, but seems to be feeding entirely of their heads, leaving the rest of the Shad bodies to be eaten by scavengers.

name: Rainbow Outlaw Mount
description: Rainbow Outlaw (Oncorhynchus Genetikus) this abnormally large specimen of a lake form Rainbow Trout was apparently sneaky enough to escape from one of Oregon’s trout farms, where it was genetically engineered to grow extra-large. The oversized runaway resorted to some meticulous route planning to make its escape - using a network of underground streams it traveled between different lakes until settling down in Falcon’s peaceful waters. But while this genetically modified organism succeeded in covering its tracks from the fish farmers, it’s huge size of over 25 kg (50 lb) is a dead giveaway. And feeding exclusively on Brown Trout Eggs, the Rainbow Outlaw is only getting bigger.

name: Terror Tarpon Mount
description: Terror Tarpon (Megalops Terroristus) looking scarred and hostile, this highly aggressive Tarpon came to the quiet marshy areas of the Everglades from the brackish coastal prairies and is terrorizing the local fish. Although relatively average in size, weighing just about 44 lb (20 kg), this feisty trouble maker is doing a lot of damage to the underwater ecosystem of this area by seriously diminishing the population of Largemouth Bass, which it seems to have a particular taste for.

name: Voodoo Fish Mount
description: Voodoo Fish (Lota Magicus) according to an old indian legend, this mythical fish belongs to an extinct species that possessed magical powers and was a distant ancestor of today’s Burbot. Apparently the last remaining specimen of its kind, this age-old monster dwells in an abysmal hole somewhere in the deepest part of White Moose Lake and comes out to roam closer to the lake’s surface every once in a blue moon! No one knows exactly how long this archaic creature has lived for, but judging form the ancient markings of Northern indigenous tribes on its back, the Voodoo Fish was a part of some magical rituals that date back to over a century!

name: Zombie Cat Mount
description: Zombie Cat (Mortuus Consumus) while all Catfish are bottom-feeding scavengers in general, and among other things may consume dead fish, this particular whiskery monster has taken such an uncomely diet to the extreme. Gravely and old, the Zombie Cat feeds exclusively on any rotten and decaying organisms it can find on the bottom of swampy Quanchkin Lake. Looking rather like a monster from a Pet Cemetery horror sequel, this consumer of death is spreading a putrid smell all around the area!

name: Muskie Golem Mount
description: Muskie Golem (Esox Stonius) - there are many fish legends among the anglers of Saint Croix Lake, one of which is about the Muskie Golem. This fish gets its name for having abnormally large and tough scales that make it look as if made of rock. The Muskie Golem is also said to be well over a hundred years old and weighs almost 35 kg (75 lb), which makes it the largest Muskie specimen in all of Saint Croix! Virtually uncatchable, as it seems to take no interest in any typical baits or lures.

name: Gourmet Striped Bass Mount
description: Gourmet Bass (Morone Gurmanius) this huge specimen is way over the size of any freshwater Bass you could hope to catch! Weighing roughly 30 kg (66 lb), the Gourmet Bass gets its size and name from its highly gourmet dietary habits. Apparently, it developed quite a taste for nutritious, protein-rich foods and will eat any molluscs it can find!

name: Albino Blackfish Mount
description: Albino Blackfish (Dallia Albineus) infected by radiation from a toxic waste leak, these specimen of otherwise black Alaska Blackfish are absolutely white in color and seem to have a particularly insatiable craving for Salmon eggs. Although these infected fish are hardly over 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) in weight, they are rather numerous and therefore present a serious problem causing much damage to the populations of Salmon species.

name: Perch Bully Mount
description: Perch Bully (Perca Corruptor) is a ferocious predator unlike any Perch you’ve ever seen! Relentlessly hunting down its prey and devouring any fish it can bite into with its big mouth and razor sharp teeth, the Perch Bully can only be caught using a special type of lure!

name: Eel Cannibal Mount
description: Cannibal Eel (Anguilla Canibalium) was smuggled into the peaceful waters of Ghent-Terneuzen canal from Africa by rebellious trouble-makers. It looks horrifying enough to scare any angler out of their wits. This monster seems to have a particular taste for its own kind, heartlessly hunting for other Eels and decimating their population!

name: Grayling Wrestler Mount
description: Grayling Wrestler (Thymallus Luctator) is a monstrous type of European Grayling with a temper so malicious that it has turned its color to dark, almost black! It’ll take some wits and skills to catch this mad fighter!

name: Ghost Peacock Bass Mount
description: Ghost Peacock Bass (Cichla Exspiravit) - this pale, red-eyed monster seems to stir quite a panic among all other fish, making it impossible for anglers to enjoy their favorite pastime at this waterway! Seen only at night, the Ghost Peacock Bass will turn anyone who catches it into a real ghostbusting hero in the eyes of the local angling community!

name: Black Whisker Mount
description: Black Whisker (Silurus Nigreos) - this huge whiskered monster has devoured so much fish in Sander Baggersee Lake, that its belly and eyes look like they are about to burst! Even so, the Black Whisker doesn't plan to stop its feeding frenzy, thus putting the lake’s entire ecosystem at risk. Not unless some fearless angler puts an end to this dark foodsie’s nightmare!

name: Sturgeon Leviathan Mount
description: Leviathan Sturgeon (Acipenseridae Pristis) is a huge monster fish found in the Dnipro River. Known for its impressive size and strength, this fish is a dream catch for adventurous anglers looking for a thrilling challenge. To reel in this unique giant, you'll need a combination of skill, a bit of luck, and some special lures.

name: Carp Colossus Mount
description: Colossus Carp (Cyprinidae Colossus) - a Carp unlike any you’ve ever seen, this colossal monstrous creature is terrorizing the peaceful waters of Weeping Willow fisheries! Even the largest trophy-sized species are terrified of this fat-bellied underwater titan, lurking in the murky depths. Will anyone find a way to lure the Colossus Carp out of its underwater lair?

name: Elusive Arapaima Mount
description: This is probably the oldest and most cunning Arapaima you can ever encounter. The local legends say that this monster is the evil spirit of Lake Maku-Maku, who has lived there since time immemorial. Anyone who tried to catch it failed at best, and at worst — disappeared altogether! They say neither tridents, nor nets, nor strong tackle can take it on. However, there is a way for a brave angler to land this ancient fish!

name: Fighter Shark Mount
description: Young sharks are known to often become prey to local caimans. However, this particular monster has won many battles with the sharp-toothed reptiles. Its hundreds of scars and the only remaining eye speak eloquently about its victories. Having gained strength and experience, the monster itself became a menace to the caimans, which are worshiped by the local tribe!

name: Wailing Catfish Mount
description: This huge and greedy catfish was nicknamed Wailing for a reason. The low sounds emitted by this giant resemble underwater growling and can be heard hundreds of meters away from the Marron River. Its cries spreading through the jungle can scare not only fish and animals, but also people. And although it’s known for certain that some catfish can make loud sounds, no ichthyologists have ever heard such a roar. Rest assured, they would give a lot to get their hands on such a specimen!

name: Mega Piranha Mount
description: Nobody knows whose evil genius combined the most voracious fish in South America with the latest achievements in biomechatronics to create incredibly powerful cyborg monsters! Razor-sharp teeth made from solid adamant, improved bodies with mechanical fins, cyber vision, and inherent bloodthirstiness — what else do ideal killer fish need? To tackle one of these monstrosities, you’ll need a miracle — or an Adamant Leader!

name: Taimen Khan Mount
description: This huge Taimen has no competitors because of its impressive size. This is an excellent hunter who is constantly on the move. This Taimen is not too picky in terms of food: it’s happy to eat rodents and waterfowl that have fallen into the water as well as small fish. According to old-timers, it once used to drag dogs into the deep. This specimen is rightfully considered the Khan of the entire Selenge River.

name: Mighty M'Benga Mount
description: Local legends say that the Congo is home to an evil spirit named M'Benga, which can possess river dwellers. It seems that this spirit has inhabited a particularly large specimen of Goliath Tigerfish. The spirit grants the monster fish demonic strength and bloodthirstiness. According to the legend, only the blood of its fellow species and a special ritual performed by a real shaman can temporarily calm the fury of M'Benga. So hurry up — you don't have much time!

name: Grouperzilla Mount
description: Grouperzilla is a creature born from the depths of the polluted oceans, where an ordinary huge grouper transformed into a giant sea monster. It’s known for its considerable size and strength, far exceeding any known representative of its species. Grouperzilla is known for its aggressive behavior and insatiable appetite. It often hunts for its favorite snack — lobsters — and can attack the boats of anglers who have this delicacy on board.

name: Striped Blade Mount
description: The Striped Blade Monster is an incredible Marlin known for its speed and aggressiveness. Its long, sword-like snout is supernaturally tough, allowing it to cut through even the strongest fishing nets. The iridescent stripes on this Monster’s body serve as a warning sign in the underwater environment, clearly indicating who’s in charge here. These stripes also emit a faint glow, which creates the impression of dancing light in the dark depths of the ocean and attracts underwater creatures. This graceful and powerful monster will become the jewel of any sophisticated collection.

name: Armored Bighead Mount
description: Armored Bighead (Hypophthalmichthys Armatus) is a giant mutated bighead carp weighing up to 150 kg(330 lbs) that has become а true terror of the waters of Sander Baggersee. In the 9th century, the Viking ship "Gormrsvein" sailed along the River Main, carrying a magical artifact - a rune-inscribed amulet capable of altering the nature of things. During a fierce storm, the ship sank, taking the amulet to the bottom of the lake. Over time, a colossal monster appeared in these waters, covered in armor-like scales that made it nearly invincible. The Armored Bighead has been spotted during its hunting raids, sinking ships and boats that cross its territory. It is believed that the creature swallowed the magical amulet, which caused its transformation, granting it incredible strength and impenetrable protection.

name: Double Head Eel Mount
description: The Double Head Eel (Anguilla Bicephalus) is a terror of the depths that frightens even the most experienced anglers. This mutated predator, weighing up to 35 kg(77 lbs), has two fully functional heads, each with its own mind and an insatiable hunger for hunting. Its snake-like body is covered in slime that releases toxins, paralyzing its prey upon contact. The Double Head Eel can attack from both sides simultaneously, making it nearly unbeatable in close combat. It breaks through underwater obstacles and attacks from unexpected angles. It is said that its appearance is always accompanied by electrical storms, as if nature itself is warning of the danger.

name: Akkorokamui Mount
description: Akkorokamui (Octopuses gigantic) is a legendary giant squid that dwells in the dark depths of the oceans. Its red body glows in the darkness, warning of the danger lurking below. This mythical squid, weighing up to 150 kg(330 lb), has enormous tentacles capable of enveloping an entire ship and dragging it into the abyss. The suckers on its tentacles can create a powerful vacuum, strong enough to tear through the toughest materials. Akkorokamui’s special ability is to release an inky cloud laced with toxins that paralyze its prey. According to legend, it is a cursed ocean spirit, doomed to guard the depths, and its appearance always foretells disaster.

name: Dingonek Mount
description: The Dingonek is a massive creature, weighing up to 155 kg(340 lbs), with a head resembling a lioness marked like a leopard, and two long white fangs protruding from its upper jaw. Its broad back, covered in armadillo-like scales, is reminiscent of a hippo's. A wide, finned tail allows it to stay afloat in swift currents. Some believe it may be a descendant of prehistoric reptiles that survived in remote regions, though no bones or skin samples have been found. Eyewitness accounts, however, leave little room for doubt.

name: Slide Rock Bolter Mount
description: The Slide-Rock Bolter (Macrostoma saxiperrumptus) is a bizarre and fearsome creature recounted by the lumberjacks of North America during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is believed to live in the mountains of Colorado. The creature has an immense head, small eyes, and a large mouth, weighing up to 160 kg(350 lbs). Its tail ends in a fluke similar to a dolphin, equipped with enormous grab-hooks. This fearsome animal uses the grab-hooks on its split tail to latch onto the crest of a mountain or ridge. Once it spots its prey, it lifts its tail to release its hold, then slides down, scooping its victims into its mouth. When not hunting, the Bolter resides in the depths of mountain lakes.

name: Vampire Biara Mount
description: Vampire Biara (Rhaphiodon vulpinus vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish, weighing up to 60 kg(132 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Biara feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

name: Vampire Payara Mount
description: Vampire Payara (Hydrolycus Scomberoides vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish that can weigh up to 90 kg(198 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Payara feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

name: Vampire Trahira Mount
description: Vampire Trahira (Hoplias Aimara vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish that can weigh up to 120 kg(264 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Trahira feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

name: Thorn-Ripper Mount
description: The Thorn-Ripper is an aggressive monster fish that lives in the depths of the Dnipro River. Its spikes grew over centuries of survival among predators, serving as both defense and weapon. Legends say that humans once fished out its family, and since then, the Thorn-Ripper has been seeking revenge on fishermen by piercing boats with its spikes. When it hears the sound of a boat above its territory, it swiftly attacks, puncturing it like needles. Fishermen now fear encountering this underwater menace. Since this fish is extremely cautious, only a unique lure like the Wasp Walker can capture its interest.

description: Nice catch! This grooved blade made of forged steel came from none other but George Washington’s battle sword that he used while serving as commander of the Continental army during the Revolutionary War.

name: Page 1 of the diary - Colorado Myster
description: In the remote corners of the Colorado mountains, there is a legend of the monster Slide-Rock Bolter, responsible for the disappearance of people for many years. Long ago, on Rocky Lake, Indian fishermen in an old canoe were eaten by this creature. Their souls remained trapped in its belly, and the canoe became a ghostly vessel, drifting across the lake. They say the Slide-Rock Bolter, resembling a whale with a massive head and hooks on its tail, could grab onto a mountain above the water, watching for prey, and swiftly swoop to devour everything in its path. Today, a Crow tribe shaman summoned the creature from the lake's depths, luring it with a mix of Fireflies and Grave Soil. I feared it might attack until the monster sank back into the depths, but the shaman's amulet protected me...

name: Page 2 of the diary - Roman Mystery
description: While traveling along a river in Italy, I noticed strange amphorae washed up on the banks. I was forbidden to even approach them. It`s said that once the captain of the Roman merchant ship "Aurelia" offended a siren, and seeking revenge, she swam into the Tiber River and cursed the local waters. As a result, ordinary eels transformed into double-headed monsters with incredible strength and a thirst for destruction. The Siren put magic spells on the eels and created illusions to confuse the crew. They attacked the captain's ship, tearing its sides and masts with powerful jaws. The ship quickly sank, taking all the cargo and crew with it. It`s rumored that the Double Head Eels have not disappeared, and the siren's magic still works. The Labradorite stone is needed to remove this spell, which was hidden long ago in an old well near an ancient manor. The monsters cannot be defeated without it...

name: Page 4 of the diary - Amazonian Mystery
description: When the vampires were banished from the Old World, they found refuge in the wild lands of South America. Legends do not retain information about what happened to their ship upon arrival, but it's known that they settled on an old steamboat. Gliding through the waters of the Amazon, they conducted their dark affairs, remaining invulnerable to the local tribes. To strengthen their defense, the vampires created monstrous vampire fish, who, as invisible guardians, attacked the locals' boats. Years passed, and the vampires themselves disappeared, leaving behind only dark memories and horrors. But the monster fish remained, tied to the ghostly ships, a reminder of that dark era when the Amazon was their territory. On misty nights, under the moon, you can hear the splash of water as the vampire fish patrol their cursed waters, forever guarding the phantom vessels of their creators...

name: Page 5 of the diary - Congo Mystery
description: A priest from one settlement had an incredibly beautiful wife. The chief of a neighboring village, filled with envy, cunningly kidnapped her, made her his third wife, and offered the priest a monkey instead. Consumed by rage, the priest decided to take revenge. He performed a dangerous ritual and summoned the saber-toothed monster Dingonek, directing it toward the chief's village to destroy it. I learned this story and its variations while staying in a village on the banks of the Congo. No one knows exactly why the two settlements quarreled. Many years have passed, but the locals still avoid the river in the middle of autumn, fearing an encounter with the monster. Sometimes, they see the ghost of a ship and hear a roar. It's mid-autumn now, and I'll go to the river tomorrow evening, hoping for a possible encounter with this mysterious creature...
